card.headline: BlueStone board approves up to ₹300 Cr NCD private placement
BlueStone board approves up to ₹300 Cr NCD private placement
card.takeaway: The company can raise up to ₹300 Cr through NCDs in one or more tranches, with terms to be set later by its Operations Committee.
card.core_catalyst: Debt refinancing and business growth funding via NCDs

what_happened.text: Board approved raising up to **₹300 Cr** through NCDs on a private placement basis, in one or more series or tranches.
what_happened.quote: The Board has accorded its approval for raising funds of up to ₹300 crore (Indian Rupees Three Hundred Crore only) through the issuance of its non-convertible debentures (“Debentures” / “NCDs”) on a private placement basis, in one or more series / tranches.

what_happened.text: Proceeds are proposed for refinancing part of existing debt and business growth needs — capital expenditure, working capital and general corporate requirements.
what_happened.quote: The proceeds of subscription of the Debentures are proposed to be utilized inter alia for refinancing a portion of its existing debt and business growth requirements (capital expenditure, working capital and general corporate requirements).

what_happened.text: The Operations Committee is authorized to determine and finalize the allotment terms and conditions of the NCDs.
what_happened.quote: The Board has authorized the Operations Committee to determine and finalize the terms and conditions of the allotment of NCDs.

what_happened.text: Regulation 30(6) disclosure will be made at the time of issuance and/or allotment of the NCDs.
what_happened.quote: The disclosure as required under the Regulation 30(6) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosures Requirements) Regulations, 2015 read with SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD PoD1/P/CIR/2023/123 dated July 13, 2023, would be made at the time of issuance and/or allotment of NCDs.

headline: IDL Explosives commissions 9,000 MT bulk explosives silo near Asansol, expanding its national network

card.headline: IDL Explosives commissions 9,000 MT bulk explosives silo near Asansol, expanding its national network
IDL Explosives commissions 9,000 MT bulk explosives silo near Asansol, expanding its national network
card.takeaway: IDL Explosives adds delivery capacity near coal mines, supporting its bulk explosives order book from Coal India subsidiaries.
card.core_catalyst: New silo capacity in the Eastern and Central Coal Belt to service long-term bulk explosives orders from Coal India subsidiaries

what_happened.text: IDL Explosives Limited, a group company of Apollo Micro Systems, commissioned the Bolkunda Silo Unit, a new bulk explosives silo plant with a capacity of **9,000 MT**, spread over **8.4 acres** near Asansol, West Bengal.
what_happened.quote: IDL Explosives Limited (“IDL”), a group company of Apollo Micro Systems Limited, has commissioned the Bolkunda Silo Unit, a new bulk explosives silo plant with a capacity of 9,000 MT, spread over 8.4 acres of land near Asansol, West Bengal.

what_happened.text: The facility was inaugurated on **22-10-2026** by Sri Baddam Karunakar Reddy, Founder and Managing Director of Apollo Micro Systems Limited.
what_happened.quote: The facility was inaugurated on 22-10-2026 by Sri Baddam Karunakar Reddy, Founder and Managing Director, Apollo Micro Systems Limited, in the presence of senior leadership of IDL, and stands dedicated to operational excellence.

what_happened.text: The unit will serve mining operations of Eastern Coalfields Limited, Central Coalfields Limited and other regional customers with site-mixed bulk explosives, and strengthens IDL's capacity to service long-term bulk explosives orders from Coal India subsidiaries.
what_happened.quote: Located in the heart of the Eastern Coal Belt and the Central Coal Belt, the Bolkunda Silo Unit will serve the mining operations of Eastern Coalfields Limited, Central Coalfields Limited and other customers in the region with site-mixed bulk explosives. The unit expands IDL Explosives' national network of bulk explosives plants and silos and strengthens its capacity to service long-term bulk explosives orders from Coal India subsidiaries.

why_it_matters.text: The filing gives no project cost, funding mix, commissioning timeline or expected revenue potential for the Bolkunda Silo Unit.
why_it_matters.quote: Located in the heart of the Eastern Coal Belt and the Central Coal Belt, the Bolkunda Silo Unit will serve the mining operations of Eastern Coalfields Limited, Central Coalfields Limited and other customers in the region with site-mixed bulk explosives.

Shakti Pumps H1FY27 revenue rose 24.5% YoY to ₹1,605 Cr; EBITDA margin fell to 9.2%
card.takeaway: Revenue momentum is intact but margins halved YoY, while operating cash flow turned sharply negative in H1FY27.
card.core_catalyst: Strong solar pump execution offset by lower realisations, higher raw material costs and elevated logistics expenses

what_happened.text: H1FY27 revenue from operations rose 24.5% YoY to ₹1,605 Cr; Q2FY27 revenue rose 12.0% YoY to ₹746 Cr.
H1FY27 EBITDA fell to ₹147 Cr from ₹280 Cr in H1FY26; margin fell to 9.2% from 21.7%; Q2FY27 margin was 8.6% versus 20.4% a year ago.
H1FY27 PAT was ₹90 Cr versus ₹188 Cr in H1FY26; Q2FY27 PAT was ₹39 Cr versus ₹91 Cr.
Order book stood at ₹751 Cr as of 23 October 2026, inclusive of GST; solar pumps installed rose 29.3% YoY to 51,543 units in H1FY27.
what_happened.quote: Our order book stood at ₹ 7,510 Mn as of 23rd October 2026.

what_happened.text: Operating cash flow turned negative at negative ₹448 Cr in H1FY27 versus positive ₹124 Cr in H1FY26.

why_it_matters.text: Margins halved YoY as management cited lower realisations, higher raw material costs and elevated logistics expenses linked to geopolitical conditions.
why_it_matters.quote: Margins during the period moderated due to lower realisations, higher raw material costs and elevated logistics expenses linked to prevailing geopolitical conditions.

why_it_matters.text: ₹17,000 Mn capex programme is underway; 0.5 GW of the planned 2.2 GW solar module capacity commenced trial production in October 2026, with the 2.2 GW DCR solar cell facility to be commissioned by FY28.
